goals.0: Saying what you and other people do for a living
goals.1: Male and female forms of jobs: Lehrer / Lehrerin
goals.2: The forms of the verb arbeiten
goals.3: “Ich bin Student” — no ein before a job
dialog.0.de.3.n: „von Beruf“ = by profession. Full sentence: What do you do for a living?
dialog.1.de.2.n: Unlike English, there is no ein before a job: Ich bin Student (not “a student”)
dialog.3.de.1.n: er arbeitet — the stem ends in t, so an e is added in the middle
dialog.4.de.2.n: im = in + dem; it shows place — more detail later
grammar.0.title: No ein before a job
grammar.0.text: In German you name a job without ein/eine: „Ich bin Lehrer.“, „Sie ist Ärztin.“ — just as in Bangla (“ami shikkhok”). The “a” of English “I am a teacher” is missing here.
grammar.1.title: Male → female: add -in
grammar.1.note: Plural of the female form: -innen (die Lehrerinnen).
grammar.2.intro: arbeiten — the stem ends in t, so du/er/ihr get an e in the middle (to make it easier to pronounce).
quiz.3.prompt: What do you call a female teacher in German?
quiz.5.why: du + arbeiten → arbeitest (an e is added).
quiz.6.why: Use sein for jobs, without ein: Ich bin Student.
quiz.7.prompt: Put the words in order: “What is your job?”
